# AI-Assisted Data Visualization with Claude Code: Comprehensive Learning Guide

## Course Overview

This course teaches you how to leverage Claude's code generation and analytical capabilities to build interactive, insightful data visualizations without writing every line of code from scratch. You'll learn to communicate data analysis requirements in natural language, refine Claude-generated code, and integrate visualizations into real-world applications.

**Who it's for:**
- Junior to mid-level developers transitioning into data roles
- Full-stack engineers looking to add visualization expertise
- Data analysts wanting to automate reporting pipelines
- Professionals preparing for technical interviews in data engineering or analytics roles

**Why it matters for interview prep:**
Modern technical interviews increasingly assess your ability to work *with* AI tools, not just write code in isolation. Mastery of this path demonstrates:
- Problem decomposition and clear communication (critical for any interview)
- Understanding of visualization principles and data storytelling
- Practical knowledge of Python, JavaScript, and modern libraries
- Ability to iterate and debug AI-assisted code intelligently
- End-to-end thinking from raw data to polished presentation

## Core Topics Covered

- **Natural Language Prompting for Code Generation** — Crafting precise requests to Claude that yield production-quality visualization code
- **Python Data Stack Integration** — Pandas, NumPy, Plotly, Matplotlib; understanding when Claude suggests which tools
- **Interactive Visualization Frameworks** — Building dashboards with Plotly, Streamlit, and Dash with Claude assistance
- **Data Transformation & Cleaning** — Using Claude to generate data pipelines and handling edge cases
- **JavaScript/Web Visualization** — D3.js, Chart.js, and Observable; translating Claude output to web contexts
- **Prompt Engineering for Analytics** — Iterating on Claude suggestions, debugging generated code, and adding custom logic
- **Statistical Visualization Patterns** — Time series, distributions, correlations, and categorical comparisons
- **Performance & Optimization** — Making Claude-generated code production-ready for large datasets

## Learning Path Workflow

### **Phase 1: Foundations (Tasks 1–9)**
Start here to understand how to work with Claude for code generation.

1. **Introduction to Claude Code Assistance** — Explore the Claude API and interface; understand tokenization and cost implications
2. **Crafting Effective Data Visualization Prompts** — Learn the anatomy of a good prompt: context, requirements, constraints, output format
3. **Python Environment Setup** — Configure Jupyter, virtual environments, and Claude API keys
4. **Your First Claude-Generated Visualization** — Create a simple scatter plot from CSV data using a well-structured prompt
5. **Reading & Modifying Claude Output** — Analyze generated code, identify patterns, spot potential issues
6. **Common Pitfalls in AI-Generated Visualization Code** — Handle library version conflicts, missing edge cases, hardcoded values
7. **Documentation & Reproducibility** — Structure notebooks to track prompts, Claude responses, and modifications
8. **Debugging Claude-Generated Code** — Systematic approaches to fixing errors in generated visualizations
9. **Ethics & Data Privacy in AI-Assisted Analysis** — Considerations when using Claude for sensitive data; output control

### **Phase 2: Core Visualization Patterns (Tasks 10–22)**
Build fluency with standard visualization types using Claude.

10. **Time Series Visualization** — Ask Claude to generate line charts with moving averages, annotations, and dual axes
11. **Distribution Analysis (Histograms & KDE)** — Prompt Claude to create multi-panel distribution comparisons
12. **Categorical Comparisons (Bar Charts)** — Generate grouped and stacked bar charts with proper sorting and labeling
13. **Correlation & Heatmaps** — Use Claude to build correlation matrices with annotations
14. **Scatter Plots & Dimensionality** — Add color, size, and transparency dimensions; request trendline overlays
15. **Box Plots & Violin Plots** — Ask Claude for statistical distribution comparisons with outlier highlighting
16. **Geographic Visualizations (Maps)** — Prompt Claude to create choropleth maps and point clusters using Folium/Plotly
17. **Interactive Dashboards with Plotly** — Request multi-chart dashboards with linked selections
18. **Streamlit Apps for Rapid Prototyping** — Use Claude to generate interactive apps with sliders and filters
19. **Custom Color Scales & Styling** — Prompt Claude for branded visualizations with consistent color palettes
20. **Animation & Transitions** — Request animated bar charts, transitions, and reveal effects
21. **3D Visualizations** — Generate surface plots, scatter plots in 3D space, and interactive rotations
22. **Network & Graph Visualizations** — Use Claude to create node-link diagrams and force-directed layouts

### **Phase 3: Advanced Techniques (Tasks 23–32)**
Integrate Claude assistance with more complex, production-grade scenarios.

23. **Combining Multiple Data Sources** — Prompt Claude to merge and pivot data, then visualize
24. **Real-Time Data Dashboards** — Generate code to stream data updates and refresh visualizations
25. **Building a Data Pipeline with Claude** — Extract → Transform → Visualize workflow
26. **A/B Testing Visualization** — Request statistical comparison charts and confidence interval plots
27. **Cohort Analysis Visualizations** — Prompt Claude for retention curves and user journey flows
28. **Financial Data Visualization** — Candlestick charts, volume bars, moving averages
29. **Machine Learning Results Visualization** — Confusion matrices, ROC curves, feature importance plots
30. **Accessibility in AI-Generated Visualizations** — Ensure color-blind friendly palettes, alt text, semantic HTML
31. **Performance Optimization for Large Datasets** — Request efficient aggregation, sampling strategies, and canvas rendering
32. **Exporting & Embedding Visualizations** — Generate code to export as PNG, SVG, HTML, or embed in reports

### **Phase 4: Integration & Interview Prep (Tasks 33–39)**
Synthesize skills into interview-ready projects.

33. **End-to-End Data Analysis Project** — Scoped problem: ingest raw data, clean with Claude assistance, generate insights with visualizations
34. **Building a Reusable Visualization Library** — Create wrapper functions around Claude suggestions to standardize outputs
35. **Debugging & Optimization in Interviews** — Practice explaining Claude code choices and iterating under time pressure
36. **Communicating with Stakeholders via Visualizations** — Generate executive dashboards and supporting narrative
37. **Handling Ambiguous Requirements** — Practice clarifying vague visualization requests into precise Claude prompts
38. **Time-Boxed Visualization Challenges** — Timed exercises mimicking interview scenarios (30–60 min projects)
39. **Capstone: Portfolio-Ready Data Project** — Full project from business question to polished visualizations and presentation

## Key Skills You'll Build

### Technical Competencies
- **Prompt Engineering** — Writing clear, specific, iterative requests that consistently yield high-quality code
- **Python Data Manipulation** — Pandas operations, groupby, merging, and reshaping (learned via Claude examples)
- **Visualization Libraries** — Proficiency with Plotly, Matplotlib, Seaborn, Streamlit, and Dash
- **JavaScript/Web Visualization** — D3.js fundamentals, Observable notebooks, and web-based interactive tools
- **SQL & Data Queries** — Generating queries with Claude for data extraction and aggregation
- **Statistical Thinking** — Understanding when to use which chart type; interpreting visual encodings

### Soft Skills & Patterns
- **Code Review & Debugging** — Critically evaluating AI-generated code before deployment
- **Iterative Refinement** — Multi-turn conversations with Claude to converge on the right solution
- **Trade-off Analysis** — Balancing interactivity, performance, and maintainability in visualization choices
- **Communication** — Explaining data stories and translating business questions into visual designs
- **Constraints & Edge Cases** — Handling missing data, outliers, and edge cases in generated code

## Sample Problem Types

### **Problem Type 1: "Generate a Dashboard for KPI Monitoring"**

**Description:** Given daily metrics data (revenue, user signups, churn rate), create an interactive dashboard showing trends, anomalies, and comparisons to target.

**Claude Prompt Example:**
```
I have daily data in a CSV with columns: date, revenue, signups, churn_rate.
Create a Streamlit dashboard with:
- KPI cards showing today's values
- Time series line charts for each metric
- A sidebar filter for date range selection
- Highlight any day where revenue is >20% below rolling 30-day average
Make it mobile-responsive and use a professional color scheme.
```
